sections.html: South America: Atlantic, Paraguay and Uruguay River basins. Reported from the upper Paraná and its tributaries in Argentina. Type locality: Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
Very small species that can probably be kept as per other members of this family, in a quiet tank with sand and plants.

Pseudobunocephalus is distinguished from all other aspredinid genera by several unique anatomical features, including mandibular teeth restricted to a patch near the symphysis of the lower jaw and the absence of gill rakers on all branchial arches. The genus name combines the Greek pseudes, meaning false or deceptive, with the aspredinid genus Bunocephalus, alluding to the fact that its members were previously mistaken for juveniles of various Bunocephalus species. The specific name iheringii honours the German-Brazilian zoologist Hermann von Ihering (1850–1930), who helped collect the type. A new species, Pseudobunocephalus timbira Leão, Carvalho, Reis & Wosiacki, 2019, has been described from streams of the lower Tocantins and Mearim river drainages in northern and northeastern Brazil. IUCN Red List: Least Concern, due to its wide range, despite limited information.
